name: City Centre and Call Lane
tagline: Victorian arcades, converted mills and the bar quarter
description: The compact core between the station and Briggate, mixing glass-roofed Victorian arcades, redbrick warehouse conversions and the bars of Call Lane and the Corn Exchange. Most of the city's coworking spaces sit here, and the train station is a five minute walk from almost any flat.
bestFor: Nomads who want coworking, bars and trains all within walking distance.
pros: Walk to every coworking space and cafe
Station on the doorstep for day trips
No car or bus pass needed
cons: Weekend nightlife noise around Call Lane
Small flats with little outdoor space

name: Chapel Allerton
tagline: Leeds' independent cafe and deli village to the north
description: A village-feel high street of independent coffee shops, delis, bookshops and small bars, surrounded by Victorian terraces and semis. It draws young professionals and families rather than students, and it is a fifteen minute bus into the centre. The best all-round choice for a longer stay.
bestFor: Longer-stay remote workers who want a proper neighbourhood with good coffee.
pros: Strong independent cafe and food scene

name: Headingley
tagline: Student heartland with a cricket ground and a long high street
description: The Otley Road corridor is lined with pubs, takeaways, charity shops and cafes, backed by streets of red-brick terraces let mostly to University of Leeds students. Rents are competitive and the bus into town is constant, but the calendar swings hard between term time and summer.
bestFor: Younger nomads on a budget who want cheap pints and easy short lets.
pros: Cheap rent and plenty of room shares
Constant buses down to the city centre
Lots of pubs, gyms and cheap food
cons: Housing stock is worn and often poorly insulated

name: Hyde Park and Woodhouse
tagline: The cheapest walkable option, right beside the universities
description: Dense back-to-back terraces between the city centre and Headingley, wrapped around Hyde Park itself and the Hyde Park Picture House cinema. It is the cheapest place you can still walk into town from, and it stays busy with students and recent graduates all year.
bestFor: Budget nomads who want the lowest rent while staying walkable to the centre.
pros: Lowest rents within walking distance of town
Park, indie cinema and cheap eats nearby
Easy to find short-term room shares
cons: Higher rates of burglary and street crime
Noisy, litter-strewn streets in term time
Old damp housing with poor heating

name: Roundhay
tagline: Big houses beside one of England's largest city parks
description: A well-off residential area northeast of the centre, built around the 700 acre Roundhay Park with its lakes, woodland and Tropical World. Housing is mostly large Victorian and interwar semis, with Street Lane providing the cafes and shops. Quiet, green and clearly car dependent.
bestFor: Remote workers or families who want space, greenery and a calm home office.
pros: Huge park for running and walking
More space for the money than the centre
cons: Twenty-five minutes or more into town
